title: Adaptive low-footprint client SDK and streaming fallback PRD (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This PRD describes an adaptive, minimal-memory client SDK for Redwood's Hosted API that prioritizes running on constrained clients (mobile, edge devices, embedded apps) while preserving streaming, tool-calling, and structured-output guarantees. It outlines API surfaces, fallback behaviors, runtime constraints, and rollout/telemetry plans. The doc focuses on ergonomics and predictable developer mental models for intermittent networks and low-memory runtimes.

Background and rationale:
- Many customers embed Redwood into mobile/native apps and lightweight browser contexts. Current SDKs assume a full-featured runtime (large buffers, background threads) which causes poor UX on low-end devices.
- There are documented support tickets where clients OOM, drop streams, or never recover when tool-calls are required under tight memory.
- We need a slim SDK variant that: (1) preserves progressive/streaming user-visible outputs, (2) exposes a deterministic tool-calling contract that supports offline buffering, (3) emits structured outputs in an incremental, resumable format, and (4) surfaces simple knobs for app developers to trade fidelity for memory/latency.

Goals:
- Deliver a "low-footprint" SDK package (~<200KB minified native shim) for iOS/Android/Web that can operate with a 2–8MB working set.
- Support streaming tokens as incremental events with optional compact framing to reduce memory.
- Define a compact tool-calling handshake that tolerates retry, queueing, and local short-term persistence (up to N seconds/minutes configurable).
- Provide a small structured-output checkpoint format that enables resume after client restart or transient network failure.
- Document developer ergonomics: patterns for partial render, progressive validation, and graceful degradation.

Non-goals:
- Not replacing full-featured SDKs or adding language idioms beyond simple JS/Swift/Kotlin shims.
- Not implementing heavy local model inference.
- Not addressing enterprise Dedicated/Private deployment policies beyond API compatibility.

Success metrics (first 90 days after alpha):
- Alpha integration on two customer apps (one iOS, one Android) with stable streaming behavior.
- Reduction in client OOM incidents related to SDK calls by 70% in the apps rolled out.
- Median time-to-first-token on low-end devices <= 250ms over typical cellular links (measured in-field).
- Instrumented successful tool-call completion rate >= 95% when network stable; graceful degradation observed otherwise.

Key UX and developer flows:
1) Progressive render (low-memory friendly):
- SDK emits "token-chunk" events which include either raw token text or a compressed token delta.
- App receives and renders visible chunks; SDK maintains only a small sliding window of recent tokens (configurable, default=512 tokens).
- For structured outputs (JSON-like), SDK emits partial frames: schema-path + value fragment + frame-id. The app can reconstruct or wait for finalization frames.

2) Tool call handshake (deterministic, resumable):
- InitiateToolCall(request) -> returns toolCallId and required capabilities.
- SDK tries to reach remote tool router; if ephemeral connectivity or memory constrained, SDK persists the minimal call descriptor to ephemeral storage (IndexedDB/NSFile/Keystore).
- Tool results stream back as "tool-frame" events attached to toolCallId. If the client restarts, the SDK can resume listening for frames if toolCallId still active (TTL controlled by server).
- If tool router is unavailable, SDK surfaces a developer callback: onToolDeferred(toolCallId, reason). App can choose to show an async placeholder.

3) Structured output checkpointing and resume:
- Checkpoint frames are compact single-line JSONL entries containing: frame-id, schema-path, partial-value (base64 if binary), last-token-offset, crc.
- SDK exposes APIs: saveCheckpoint(label) and resumeFromCheckpoint(label).
- Server will keep ephemeral session state for resumed sessions for a short TTL (default 10 minutes) to enable quick recovery without full re-run.

API surface (minimal):
- createClient({apiKey, mode: 'low-footprint', slidingWindowTokens?: number, checkpointStore?: 'auto'|'none'}) -> client
- client.startStream({prompt, structuredSchema?: string, toolHints?: []}) -> streamHandle
- streamHandle.on('chunk', (chunkMeta, textOrFragment) => {})
- streamHandle.on('tool-request', (toolCallDescriptor) => { /* return accept/queue/decline */ })
- streamHandle.on('checkpoint', (checkpointId) => {})
- client.saveCheckpoint(id) / client.resumeCheckpoint(id)
- client.shutdown() // flushes durable small state and releases buffers

SDK ergonomics & memory strategies:
- Single-threaded, event-driven core: avoid background worker(s) by default. Background polling is opt-in.
- Fixed-size ring buffers for tokens and frame metadata; allocate once at init.
- Optional compact framing: provide two encodings for chunks — human-readable (for dev mode) and compact binary-framed base64 payloads (for low-footprint mode).
- Lazy tool descriptors: the SDK only keeps a pointer to ephemeral storage unless the app opts into full in-memory copies.
- Deterministic GC hooks: client.allowImmediateRelease(path) to hint SDK to drop cached fragments for schema paths.

Network/offline behavior and fallback modes:
- Online+low-memory: stream normally using compact frames and small sliding buffer.
- Intermittent connectivity: SDK buffers minimal checkpoint and pushes tool-call metadata; if push fails, it switches to "deferred" mode and retries with exponential backoff and jitter.
- Offline: app gets a onOffline callback; SDK will optionally persist the checkpoint and provide a resume token.
- Bandwidth-constrained: SDK can switch to reduced-fidelity tokens (skip low-value tokens like filler words) - enabled by a server flag and SDK knob: fidelityLevel: high|medium|low.

Server contracts and compatibility:
- API endpoints must accept compact frames and support session resume by resume-token/toolCallId.
- TTL semantics: resume tokens, toolCallId state, and server-side partial outputs live for a configurable TTL; default dates used: resume TTL=10 minutes, tool-call result TTL=30 minutes.
- Backward compatibility: if server lacks compact framing support, SDK falls back to verbose chunking but keeps low-memory behavior by shrinking sliding windows.

Observability & telemetry (privacy mindful):
- Telemetry events (configurable off by default): stream_start, token_rate, tool_call_initiated, tool_call_completed, checkpoint_saved, resume_attempted, oom_guard_triggered.
- Payloads exclude user content; include only sizes, timing, error codes, and anonymized session feature flags.
- Expose a lightweight dev-mode profiler that logs memory high-water marks to help partners tune sliding window size.

Rollout plan:
- Alpha (4 weeks): internal SDK variant, instrumented in 2 partner apps, test on device matrix including low-end Android (1GB RAM) and iOS SE.
- Beta (8 weeks): publish JS/Swift/Kotlin artifacts with explicit opt-in flag. Add server-side compact-frame support and resume TTL config UI.
- GA (16 weeks): default packaging in Redwood SDK distribution with docs and migration guide.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- TTL values: server-side default TTL may be insufficient for some disconnected-first apps. Consider longer TTL or customer-specific policies.
- Security of persisted checkpoints on-device (encrypted at rest?). Recommend optional local encryption delegated to app.
- Monitoring: how to correlate checkpoint resume events with server-side session state without leaking content? Need a hashed correlation id.

Developer docs / sample patterns to ship with SDK:
- Pattern A: Progressive summary card that updates with each checkpoint frame.
- Pattern B: Tool-call placeholder UX with auto-resume: show spinner + last-known fragment, then stitch in tool-frame results.
- Pattern C: Offline-first note-taking: queue prompts locally and resume streaming when network returns using resume tokens.

Dependencies and risks:
- Requires lightweight on-server support for compact frame parsing and resume endpoints.
- Risk: too-small sliding windows may increase server requests/re-runs; we will measure token churn rate.
- Operational: increases short-lived session state on servers; we must monitor memory and eviction rates.

Next steps:
- Align with serving-runtime on compact-frame wire format and tool-callId TTLs. (Owners: Maya + Lin)
- Prototype JS shim and run microbenchmarks for memory with fidelity toggles. (Owner: Diego)
- Create 2 partner integration tickets and schedule alpha release.

Appendix: compact framing sketch (informal)
- Human chunk: {type: 'chunk', text: '...'}
- Compact chunk: [C, frameId, deltaOffset, payloadBase64, crc] // binary-framed encoded as base64 for transport
- Tool frame: [T, toolCallId, seq, payloadBase64, statusCode]

Document notes: this is a working PRD and expected to be iterated with eng and product. The aim is to produce a small, predictable, and ergonomic surface for constrained clients without compromising server-side guarantees for streaming, tool-calls, or structured output.
